subject: Electrical Engineering
title: CMOS: The Logic Family That Won
description: A fast breakdown of CMOS: The Logic Family That Won for builders.

hook.text: CMOS pairs NMOS and PMOS transistors so one is always off. Almost zero power when idle.

buildup.text: In a CMOS inverter, input high turns on NMOS and off PMOS. Input low does the reverse.

discovery.text: Power is consumed only during switching — not while holding a state. This was revolutionary.

twist.text: At billions of transistors, even tiny leakage currents add up. Managing leakage is a major challenge.

climax.text: Nearly every digital chip made today — from watches to supercomputers — uses CMOS.

punchline.text: One on, one off — CMOS wastes almost nothing while it waits.

quiz.question: Why does CMOS consume very little power when idle?
options: Both transistors are off when the circuit is idle
One transistor is always off, blocking the path from supply to ground
CMOS uses lower supply voltages than other logic families
